content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The bug is a classic Rust gotcha: `std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` reads the **runtime** environment, but `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` is a Cargo-injected variable that only exists during `cargo build`/`cargo run`. Once the binary is installed to `~/.cargo/bin/` and invoked from a shell, that var is gone. To bake the build-time path into the binary you need the **`env!` macro**, which is evaluated at compile time and inlined as a string literal. The doc comment at line 240 even says "baked in at" — intent was right, code drifted.

The walk-up from `~/.cargo/bin/i-dream` traverses `~/.cargo`, `~/`, `/Users`, `/` — none contain `tools/menubar/build.sh`, so it fails.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Fix: switch the runtime `env::var` to the compile-time `env!` macro, and add CWD walk-up as a third fallback (so the binary still works if relocated to a different checkout).

content.text:
Fixed. The CLI now resolves project root correctly. Verified by running `i-dream widget status` — it reports build info instead of bailing.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Note the staleness detector is working too — it's telling you the Swift source has drifted since 2026-05-01 (commit `f97d627`). The fix above only restored the CLI's ability to *find* the project; rebuilding the Swift menubar app itself is a separate step. Run `i-dream widget build` (or `bash tools/menubar/build.sh`) from anywhere to refresh.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Summary:** Replaced `std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` (runtime — empty for installed binaries) with `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` (compile-time, baked into the binary) at `src/widget.rs:241`, and added a CWD walk-up as a third fallback. Reinstalled via `cargo install --path .`. Next: `i-dream widget build` to refresh the Swift app.
